# Cross-Exchange Liquidity Commentary – 2026-08-05

The liquidity hierarchy splits into three distinct tiers. NYSE and Nasdaq 100 command the top tier, with NYSE posting the lowest Amihud ILLIQ at 0.0058% per $1M traded despite a wider 0.6473% AR spread, while Nasdaq 100 achieves the tightest spreads at 0.8562% paired with stellar turnover of 1.1268%, supported by comparable volume of $354.2M. The mid-tier comprises Tokyo Stock Exchange, Euronext, SIX Swiss Exchange, and Hong Kong Stock Exchange, though TSX's elevated turnover ratio of 3.1629% and comparable volume of $56.1M signal concentrated trading activity that masks underlying price impact. Euronext offers a compelling liquidity profile with tight 0.5670% spreads and modest ILLIQ of 0.0300% per $1M, yet its comparable volume of only $11.0M signals structural fragmentation. The laggard tier—London Stock Exchange, Xetra, and Korea Exchange—shows pronounced divergences: LSE's ILLIQ deteriorates to 0.0806% per $1M despite reasonable 0.7869% spreads, while Korea Exchange suffers both highest ILLIQ at 0.1585% per $1M and widest spreads at 1.5242%, rendering it substantially less liquid across all metrics.
